why: Quote is real and the cited line is accurate, but the CONSEQUENCE is false. (1) setup.md:246 reads verbatim 'The `minimumVersion` setting establishes a floor.' and the rest of that two-sentence line plus :260 support the claimed behaviour, so the finding is not refuted on the quote. (2) packages/shared/src/config/managed-version-gate.ts:89-94 does declare only requiredMinimumVersion/requiredMaximumVersion, and `grep -an minimumVersion` over packages/*/src apps/*/src scripts returns exactly one hit -- a doc-quote comment at managed-version-gate.ts:12 that itself names the distinction ('Differs from `minimumVersion`, which prevents downgrades but never blocks startup'). So the identifier really is unwired. (3) But 'nothing constrains what the updater is allowed to install' is wrong. Our updater is electron-updater (apps/electron/src/main/auto-update.ts). Its allowDowngrade defaults to false (node_modules/electron-updater/out/AppUpdater.js:138) and isUpdateAvailable returns true only when gt(latest,current), otherwise `allowDowngrade && lt(...)` -> false (AppUpdater.js:356-362). Nothing in our source sets allowDowngrade, allowPrerelease, or autoUpdater.channel -- the channel setter is the one thing that would flip allowDowngrade to true (AppUpdater.js:33-45) -- verified with grep -an over apps/electron/src, packages/*/src, apps/cli/src (zero hits). Both the background check and the manual 'Check Now' go through the same gate (checkForUpdates at auto-update.ts:327-370 calls autoUpdater.checkForUpdates), and installUpdate() (:381) only ever installs what that gate accepted. The floor therefore exists: it is the running version, enforced by construction instead of by a settings key. Layer up: the mechanism Claude's minimumVersion exists to guard -- a runtime 'latest' -> 'stable' switch that would downgrade you (setup.md:246, :248) -- has no analogue here. The channel is baked into the artifact at build time (apps/electron/electron-builder.yml:80 `channel: "${env.NESSY_DESKTOP_UPDATE_CHANNEL}"`, set at .gitlab-ci.yml:235); there is no autoUpdatesChannel setting, no /config channel switch, and no `claude update`-equivalent manual installer (apps/cli has no self-update path). Layer down: the residual capability -- an admin-pinned floor ABOVE the running version -- is what the IMPLEMENTED requiredMinimumVersion startup gate already delivers, by refusing to start below the org minimum; the doc itself (setup.md:261) points admins at exactly those two keys for enforcement. Product difference: setup.md is CLI-installation surface (npm/native installer, Homebrew, WinGet, apt/dnf/apk, `claude update`, ~/.claude/settings.json autoUpdatesChannel); this fork ships a signed Electron .dmg/NSIS/AppImage from a corporate S3/R2 feed (scripts/prepare-release-assets.mjs, scripts/verify-update-feed.mjs), and docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-31-claude-coverage-map.md:268 already records row 152 `setup` as out of product. Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 -- none of those nine touches update/version gating -- but the coverage-map verdict is a recorded scope decision for this page.
correctedState: Partially implemented by a different mechanism, and the stated consequence does not hold. Our managed-settings version gate (packages/shared/src/config/managed-version-gate.ts) implements only the start-up range check (requiredMinimumVersion/requiredMaximumVersion), and no key named minimumVersion is read anywhere. However, the updater is NOT unconstrained: apps/electron/src/main/auto-update.ts drives electron-updater with allowDowngrade left at its false default and autoUpdater.channel never set at runtime, so isUpdateAvailable only accepts a feed version strictly greater than the running one -- both the background check and the manual check refuse to install anything below the current build. The release channel is a build-time property of the artifact (electron-builder.yml:80 / .gitlab-ci.yml:235), so the runtime channel switch that Claude's minimumVersion exists to protect against does not exist here. The only genuinely absent capability is an admin-configurable floor ABOVE the running version, and the implemented requiredMinimumVersion startup gate already covers the org-enforcement half of it.
